21.34.0.en: But David could not go before it to enquire of God: for he was afraid because of the sword of the angel of the LORD. [30]

21.34.1.en: These two verses [29-30] explain the reason for transferring that worship to Jerusalem from Gibeon, where the tabernacle was, before which they used to enquire of the Lord (1 Chr 16:39-40; Ex 29:42) [22].

21.34.2.en: What concerns the writer here is that this trial is connected with the choice of the site of the temple that Solomon the son of David would build (1 Chr 21:18; 2 Chr 1; Gen 22:2).

21.34.4.en: v My God, my soul trembles lest it fall into weakness!

21.34.5.en: David, who walked after Your heart, was deceived by Satan, so he ignored for a time Your care for him, and sent the commander of his army to number those able to go to war!

21.34.6.en: Had he forgotten the day he stood before Goliath the giant, a boy carrying nothing but a sling?!

21.34.7.en: Keep me from the thoughts of the devil and his deceptions.

21.34.8.en: Protect me by Your grace, that I may not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.

21.34.9.en: v David could not bear to see his people destroyed because of his sin.

21.34.10.en: From the depths of his heart he asked that the punishment fall on him and on his father’s house.

21.34.11.en: You looked upon the cries of his heart and his tears.

21.34.12.en: You gazed upon his heart, which loved his people more than he loved himself and his father’s house.

21.34.13.en: Give me the heart of David and a double portion of his spirit!

21.34.14.en: I do not ask selfishly for myself and my family, but I ask for all the people, indeed for all mankind.

21.34.15.en: Gladden my heart with the salvation of many.

21.34.16.en: When shall I accompany You in Your love for mankind?

21.34.17.en: Then I will look continually upon Your Cross.

21.34.18.en: And I will wait in hope for the earth and the fulness thereof to become Yours, O Savior of the world!

26.0.s.en: 1. The porters, or guards of the temple

26.0.0.en: 1 Concerning the divisions of the porters: Of the Korhites was Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph. 2 And the sons of Meshelemiah were, Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth, 3 Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Elioenai the seventh. 4 Moreover the sons of Obed-edom were, Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, and Sacar the fourth, and Nethaneel the fifth, 5 Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peulthai the eighth: for God blessed him. 6 Also unto Shemaiah his son were sons born, that ruled throughout the house of their father: for they were mighty men of valour. 7 The sons of Shemaiah; Othni, and Rephael, and Obed, Elzabad, whose brethren were strong men, Elihu, and Semachiah. 8 All these of the sons of Obed-edom: they and their sons and their brethren, able men for strength for the service, were threescore and two of Obed-edom. 9 And Meshelemiah had sons and brethren, strong men, eighteen. 10 Also Hosah, of the children of Merari, had sons; Simri the chief, (for though he was not the firstborn, yet his father made him the chief;) 11 Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth: all the sons and brethren of Hosah were thirteen. 12 Among these were the divisions of the porters, even among the chief men, having wards one against another, to minister in the house of the LORD. 13 And they cast lots, as well the small as the great, according to the house of their fathers, for every gate. 14 And the lot eastward fell to Shelemiah. Then for Zechariah his son, a wise counsellor, they cast lots; and his lot came out northward. 15 To Obed-edom southward; and to his sons the house of Asuppim. 16 To Shuppim and Hosah the lot came forth westward, with the gate Shallecheth, by the causeway of the going up, ward against ward. 17 Eastward were six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and toward Asuppim two and two. 18 At Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar. 19 These are the divisions of the porters among the sons of Kore, and among the sons of Merari.

26.0.1.en: Great buildings must be guarded, especially the temple with all its resources and its gold and silver furnishings and the gifts generously offered to it, especially after the return from the captivity. Here he speaks of the guards or porters as a group of the Levites (see 1 Chr 9:17-27), since they play a vital role in worship; for they keep the temple from the entrance of everything unfit for the holiness of the house of the Lord, besides their watchful guarding, while keeping the doors open for the priests to enter.

26.0.2.en: The porters had their important role, and they had to bear characteristics or qualities like those of the priests (1 Chr 9:13). It is fitting for them to be marked by humility and self-denial, together with holy zeal, and courage together with strength.

26.0.3.en: Their work does not stop at guarding, for the Psalms bear witness to their work in the temple as a kind of worship. As an example it is written in the Psalm: [Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in...] (Ps 24:7 etc.).

26.0.4.en: Concerning the divisions of the porters: Of the Korhites was

26.0.5.en: Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph. [1]

26.0.6.en: The list given here of the porters is the most detailed of the three lists of the porters (1 Chr 9:17-27; 16:36-42). There were four thousand guards of the temple (1 Chr 23:4-5). They were called porters, all of them Levites. Some may think that the work of the porters is lowly and of no value; yet the porters in the service of the temple have their vital role. For they carry out many other works, among them: 1. Guarding the entrances of the temple and all the roads leading to the temple. They are responsible for the sanctity of the temple, and they do not allow anything to enter that would defile the temple. 2. Opening and closing all the outer doors and watching over them, not only on official occasions, but also in the service, in order to direct those entering for worship in the courts of the sanctuary with due propriety, and to encourage the penitents, and to turn away strangers and the unclean, and to guard the temple from thieves and others who are enemies of the house of God; and in this there is a hint of the priests of the New Testament, who were entrusted with the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, to bind and to loose according to the law of the Lord Christ (Mt 16:19). 3. Examining the tools and vessels that were used every day, and making sure they were returned to their places. 4. Taking care of the furnishings of the temple and doing the cleaning work, and preparing the offerings for the sacrifices. 5. Mixing the incense that was burned daily.

26.0.7.en: The first guard that Holy Scripture records for us took place after the fall of Adam, for it is said: “So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life” (Gen 3:24).

26.0.8.en: If the temple of Solomon needed strict guarding to keep anything unclean from entering it, then there must be no laxity concerning the holiness of the Church of the Lord Christ, who redeemed her with His precious blood, and sent to her His Holy Spirit that she may be sanctified and prepared for the heavenly wedding! And the believer, as a member of the holy Church, since he carries treasures in his depths, needs strict heavenly guarding. Therefore he cries out every morning, saying: “Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips” (Ps 141:3).

26.0.9.en: The godly Levites can guard the doors of the temple and its treasures and keep it clean, but who can guard my inner mouth and the senses of my soul and cleanse my depths from every sin except You? My depths cry out: “Except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain” (Ps 127:1). You alone have established Your kingdom in me, and made me a temple for You; O Lord, arise to guard me, for I am Yours, and the enemy of good does not cease attacking me and plundering Your treasures from within me!

26.0.10.en: v We must bridle the tongue, so that it does not run to excess in the folly of speech. And when it speaks to profit, then it ought not to be silent through sloth. The prophet contemplated this matter and said: “Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips” (Ps 141:3). Here the psalmist did not ask the Lord to set a fence or a wall, but a door that can be opened or closed. Let us learn when to open our mouths wisely and at the proper time, and, on the contrary, how to close them with silence [1].

26.1.0.en: v He did not say [a strong barrier], but [a strong door] (LXX). For a door is opened as it is also closed. If it is a door, let it be opened and closed. It is opened for the confession of sin, and closed when a justification of sin is offered. So let it be a strong door, and not a door of destruction [2].

26.1.1.en: v [Except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain] (Ps 127:1)... We guard you in our work as stewards of God, but we also desire to be guarded together with you.

26.1.2.en: We are, as it were, shepherds to you, but we are also in the care of God, for we are fellow sheep with you.

26.1.3.en: We are teachers to you, but as for God, He is the one Master, and we are your fellows in His school.

26.1.4.en: If we want God to guard us, He who humbled Himself for our sake and was glorified in order to keep us, let us also humble ourselves. Let no one think that he is something, for no one has anything good unless he has received it from God, who alone is good.

26.2.0.en: v This is the house that we build by a virtuous, living life, and that God builds by His help to us that we may live a virtuous life, for “Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it” (Ps 127:1) [3].

26.3.0.en: St. Augustine v Why do you suffer, because we have no house, no shelter and no people? Is it not better for us to dwell in the builder of our house and under the guard of the keeper of our town? For if David had no place of rest until he found it (God found his rest), how can we seek rest outside Him [4]?

26.3.1.en: St. John Saba v God has placed all the resistance of Satan within the limits of the capacity of man’s will and freedom, but He has not given man complete power by which he can master his psychological passions and desires, therefore he said: “Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain” (Ps 1:127).

26.4.0.en: And the sons of Meshelemiah were,

26.4.1.en: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth, [2]

26.5.0.en: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Elioenai the seventh. [3]

26.6.0.en: Moreover the sons of Obed-edom were,

26.6.1.en: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, and Sacar the fourth, and Nethaneel the fifth, [4]

26.7.0.en: Obed-edom: Among the most prominent figures among the porters was Obed-edom with his family. He had sixty-two of his sons and their brethren; it is said that God blessed him [5].

26.7.1.en: The ark was kept in the house of Obed-edom after the death of Uzzah. God did not forget his devotion and faithfulness (1 Chr 13:14; 16:38). He became its guard when David brought it up to Jerusalem. And here we see him with his large family as guards of the gates of the temple in the time of Solomon. It is said of his sons that they were mighty men of valour, with strength for the service.

26.8.0.en: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peulthai the eighth:

26.8.2.en: Sixty-two of the sons of Obed-edom were employed in this office, he who had hosted the ark of the covenant with reverence and joy, and therefore he was rewarded well: 1. God blessed him with eight sons [5], for children are an heritage of the Lord. It is a great blessing for a family to have many sons, especially if they are able and skilled in the service of the Lord. 2. His sons were raised to places of trusted service in the sanctuary, for since they were faithful in the service of the ark of the covenant in their house, they were called to serve it in the house of God. For he who keeps God’s holy things in his house is qualified to keep them in the house of God (1 Tim 3:4-5), and David says in the Psalm: [I have kept thy law, O LORD; this I had, because I kept thy precepts] (Ps 119:55-56).

26.9.0.en: Also unto Shemaiah his son were sons born, that ruled throughout the house of their father: for they were mighty men of valour. [6]

26.10.0.en: The sons of Shemaiah; Othni, and Rephael, and Obed, Elzabad, whose brethren were strong men,

26.11.0.en: All these of the sons of Obed-edom: they and their sons and their brethren, able men for strength for the service, were threescore and two of Obed-edom. [8]

26.12.0.en: And Meshelemiah had sons and brethren, strong men, eighteen. [9]

26.13.0.en: Also Hosah, of the children of Merari, had sons;

26.13.1.en: Simri the chief, (for though he was not the firstborn, yet his father made him the chief;) [10]

26.13.2.en: It is said of one of them: “for though he was not the firstborn, yet his father made him the chief” [10], because he was outstanding, or because his elder brother was very weak, so his father made him chief, perhaps not in the inheritance [which would be contrary to the Law: (Deut 21:16-17)], but for this service which required personal qualifications.

26.14.0.en: Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth:

26.14.1.en: all the sons and brethren of Hosah were thirteen. [11]

26.15.0.en: Among these were the divisions of the porters, even among the chief men, having wards one against another, to minister in the house of the LORD. [12]

26.16.0.en: And they cast lots, as well the small as the great, according to the house of their fathers, for every gate. [13]

26.16.1.en: The porters and the singers were appointed by casting lots, each having his gate or his place [13], and it is not mentioned that they were appointed in twenty-four divisions as at the first, but their names here are twenty-four, and their divisions also are twenty-four, therefore it is believed that they were twenty-four divisions. And happy are those who dwell in the house of the Lord, for just as they are fed and taught and well employed, so they are also guarded; for men took care of the gates of the temple, but angels are at the gates of the new Jerusalem (Rev 21:12).

26.17.0.en: And the lot eastward fell to Shelemiah.

26.17.1.en: Then for Zechariah his son, a wise counsellor, they cast lots; and his lot came out northward. [14]

26.17.2.en: It is noticed that many of those called to this service were mighty men of valour [6], and men of strength [7], and able men for strength [8], and one of them was a wise counsellor [14]; and since he became a good deacon and showed extraordinary wisdom, he purchased to himself a good degree (1 Tim 3:13) and was raised from the gate to the council of counsellors; as for those who excelled in bodily strength and courage and presence of mind, they were qualified for the tasks assigned to them, for when God calls someone to service, He either finds him qualified or Himself qualifies him for it.

26.18.0.en: To Obed-edom southward; and to his sons the house of Asuppim. [15]

26.19.0.en: To Shuppim and Hosah the lot came forth westward, with the gate Shallecheth, by the causeway of the going up, ward against ward. [16]

26.20.2.en: southward four a day, and toward Asuppim two and two. [17]

26.21.0.en: At Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar. [18]

26.22.0.en: These are the divisions of the porters among the sons of Kore, and among the sons of Merari. [19]

26.23.0.en: 20 And of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of the house of God, and over the treasures of the dedicated things. 21 As concerning the sons of Laadan; the sons of the Gershonite Laadan, chief fathers, even of Laadan the Gershonite, were Jehieli. 22 The sons of Jehieli; Zetham, and Joel his brother, which were over the treasures of the house of the LORD. 23 Of the Amramites, and the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites: 24 And Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler of the treasures. 25 And his brethren by Eliezer; Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son. 26 Which Shelomith and his brethren were over all the treasures of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the chief fathers, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the host, had dedicated. 27 Out of the spoils won in battles did they dedicate to maintain the house of the LORD. 28 And all that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah, had dedicated; and whosoever had dedicated any thing, it was under the hand of Shelomith, and of his brethren.

26.23.1.en: And of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of the house of God, and over the treasures of the dedicated things. [20]

26.23.2.en: Some of the Levites were appointed to guard the treasures of the temple and the spoils and the freewill offerings. They also supervise the preparation of the sacrifices and their preservation, and keep the accounts of the gifts offered.

26.23.3.en: They keep the treasures so that neither rust nor moth corrupts them and thieves do not break in and steal, and they spend from them as needed without extravagance or reduction or squandering, and perhaps they recorded what came in and went out.

26.23.4.en: There were treasures of the house of God, for the house was great and could not be managed without various treasuries. Much of the flour for the altar and wine and oil and salt and fuel, besides the lamps, was spent daily, so quantities like these were stored up beforehand, in addition to the garments and the holy vessels; these were the storehouses of the house of God. And since money is needed to buy everything, without doubt much of it came from the offerings of the people, and perhaps much of it was set aside for necessity, and these treasuries signify the abundance in the house of the heavenly Father, for in it there is sufficiency and more than enough; for in Christ (the true temple) are the treasures of wisdom and knowledge and unsearchable riches.

26.24.0.en: As concerning the sons of Laadan; the sons of the Gershonite Laadan, chief fathers, even of Laadan the Gershonite, were Jehieli. [21]

26.25.0.en: The sons of Jehieli; Zetham, and Joel his brother, which were over the treasures of the house of the LORD. [22]

26.25.1.en: Zetham and Joel his brother, with Shebuel and Shelomith, form a committee charged with watching over the public treasuries, a committee similar to the one in the days of Nehemiah (Neh 13:13; Ezra 8:33).

26.25.2.en: The sons of Obed-edom had the responsibility of guarding the storehouses. The next prominent figures are Shelomith and his brethren, for they were responsible for all the treasures of the dedicated things which King David and the chief fathers and the captains of the armies had dedicated.

26.26.0.en: Of the Amramites, and the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites: [23]

26.27.0.en: And Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler of the treasures. [24]

26.28.0.en: And his brethren by Eliezer; Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son. [25]

26.29.0.en: Which Shelomith and his brethren were over all the treasures of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the chief fathers, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the host, had dedicated. [26]

26.30.0.en: Out of the spoils won in battles did they dedicate to maintain the house of the LORD. [27]

26.30.1.en: The spoils of war were primarily the share of the victorious army, but some of the soldiers used to offer their share to the temple, as an expression of their consecration to God.

26.30.2.en: There were treasuries for the things that were dedicated from the wars and the spoils [27] as an acknowledgment and thanksgiving for divine protection. Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth of the spoils (Heb 7:4), and in the days of Moses the men of war, when they returned victorious, offered an oblation to the Lord from their spoils. Afterward this blessed custom was revived, and not only Samuel and David, but also Abner and Joab dedicated from their spoils to maintain the house of the Lord [28], for in works of righteousness and goodness God expects from us much of what He bestows upon us, for great success calls for a corresponding return.

26.31.0.en: And all that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah, had dedicated; and whosoever had dedicated any thing, it was under the hand of Shelomith, and of his brethren. [28]

26.32.0.en: 29 Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges. 30 And of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brethren, men of valour, a thousand and seven hundred, were officers among them of Israel on this side Jordan westward in all the business of the LORD, and in the service of the king. 31 Among the Hebronites was Jerijah the chief, even among the Hebronites, according to the generations of his fathers. In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were sought for, and there were found among them mighty men of valour at Jazer of Gilead. 32 And his brethren, men of valour, were two thousand and seven hundred chief fathers, whom king David made rulers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh, for every matter pertaining to God, and affairs of the king.

26.32.1.en: The last chapter of (1 Chr 26) speaks of the role of the Levites in their relation to the people, for some of them were appointed as public officials to serve the people and the king, and also to carry out other official works, and to collect the temple’s share from them, together with attention to the ministry of teaching. Judges were also appointed throughout the land to carry out judicial work and to take care of administering justice.

26.33.0.en: 107 thousand were appointed to work west of the Jordan River, and 2700 to work on the eastern side of the Jordan in Gilead. They are put in charge of every matter pertaining to God and the affairs of the king [32]. They received special distinction, and were in contact with King David.

26.33.1.en: God’s purpose at first was that Israel should be a theocratic nation ruled by God. The tabernacle of the congregation was in the midst of the people, and the priests derived their decisions from God. But this changed because of the failure of the Levites, so God raised up judges for them. But the people asked for a king, and this led to David now being on the throne, and although the state of Israel had become a monarchy, David concentrated on bringing it back under the authority of God.

26.33.2.en: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges [29]

26.33.3.en: Here we see an account of those who were employed as officers and judges for the outward business, which must not be neglected, for rulers are appointed by God for the benefit of the Church, as are the ministers also.

26.33.4.en: The Levites were employed in the administration of justice alongside the leaders and heads of the tribes because of their knowledge of the laws more than anyone else, for this was the subject of their study.

26.34.0.en: And of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brethren, men of valour, a thousand and seven hundred, were officers among them of Israel on this side Jordan westward in all the business of the LORD, and in the service of the king. [30]

26.34.1.en: Their task was in all the business of the LORD and the service of the king [30, 32], so they managed the affairs of the country both ecclesiastically and civilly, such as God’s tithes and the king’s taxes, and punishing crimes committed against God and His honor or against the government and the peace of the people, and guarding against idolatry and acts of injustice and carrying out the laws concerning them. It is probable that some of them took care of religious matters, and others of civil matters, and by their cooperation together good service was rendered to God and the king.

26.35.0.en: Among the Hebronites was Jerijah the chief, even among the Hebronites, according to the generations of his fathers.

26.35.1.en: In the fourth (fortieth) year of the reign of David they were sought for, and there were found among them mighty men of valour at Jazer of Gilead. [31]

26.35.2.en: This organization, like the previous arrangements, was made in the fortieth year of the reign of David, that is, at the end of his reign.

26.36.0.en: And his brethren, men of valour, were two thousand and seven hundred chief fathers,

26.36.1.en: whom king David made rulers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh, for every matter pertaining to God, and affairs of the king. [32]

26.36.2.en: The number of Levites put in charge of the two and a half tribes on the eastern bank of the Jordan was 2700, that is, more than those put in charge of the rest of the tribes on the western bank of the Jordan (1700), as mentioned in (vv. 30, 32). The reason for this is either that those tribes did not have a sufficient number of judges of their own, or because of their distance from Jerusalem on the borders of the neighboring nations, so they were more exposed to the danger of contagion of idol worship, and therefore they needed a greater number of Levites to protect them.

26.36.3.en: Set, O Lord, a guard over my depths

26.36.4.en: v King David appointed godly porters and mighty men of valour, who guard the entrances of the temple, and open its doors and close them.

26.36.5.en: So that nothing unclean may enter Your sanctuary.

26.36.6.en: And no one may plunder the treasures of the temple and its goods.

26.36.7.en: In Your love You established me as a temple for You, and Your Holy Spirit dwells in me.

26.36.8.en: Do not cease pouring out Your treasures into my depths.

26.36.9.en: Who can guard my senses and my emotions and my thoughts except You?

26.36.10.en: You open and no one shuts, and You shut and no one opens.

26.36.11.en: Guard me by Your grace, that nothing foreign to You may enter my heart.

26.36.12.en: Surround me with heavenly guarding, that the enemy may not plunder Your gifts and Your treasures from me.

26.36.13.en: You set angels at the gates of the Jerusalem above (Rev 21:12).

26.36.14.en: Behold, my heart is Your Jerusalem and Your dwelling place; let angels arise to guard it until I cross over to You in peace!

26.36.15.en: v King David appointed keepers of the storehouses to oversee them.

26.36.16.en: They receive the offerings and the gifts, in order to receive the spoils of war, of gold and silver, for the temple.

26.36.17.en: They keep the garments of service and the holy vessels.

26.36.18.en: They keep the treasures so that neither rust nor moth corrupts them, and thieves do not break in and steal.

26.36.19.en: Grant me Your wisdom, that I may deposit what I am able with my brethren, the poor and the needy and the suffering.

26.36.20.en: They keep it for me, and I will recover it multiplied on the last day!

26.36.21.en: v Count me, O Lord, among the officers, that I may serve Your people.

26.36.22.en: May I seek what is for the edification of Your Church, not what is for my own profit.

26.36.23.en: I long that justice and righteousness may prevail in the midst of all Your people.

26.36.24.en: Behold, I am in Your hands; tell me: what shall I do?!

26.36.25.en: Guide me, sanctify me, and uphold me in every good work.
